front: Which IEC 61131-3 language represents a program as a graphical diagram based on the circuit diagrams of relay logic hardware?
back: Ladder Diagram (LD), also called ladder logic.
excerpt: Ladder logic has evolved into a programming language that represents a program by a graphical diagram based on the circuit diagrams of relay logic hardware.

front: How does a Function Block Diagram (FBD) describe the function between input and output variables?
back: As a set of elementary blocks, with the input and output variables joined to the blocks by connection lines.
excerpt: A function is described as a set of elementary blocks. Input and output variables are connected to blocks by connection lines.

front: What kind of language is Structured Text (ST) in IEC 61131-3?
back: A high-level, block-structured text language whose syntax resembles Pascal, on which it is based.
excerpt: It is a high-level language that is block structured and syntactically resembles Pascal, on which it is based.
mnemonic: The name spells it out: TEXT you type, STRUCTURED into blocks such as IF-THEN-ELSE. Think of Pascal, the tidy classroom language.

front: Which IEC 61131-3 language is a low-level language that resembles assembly?
excerpt: It is a low level language and resembles assembly.
mnemonic: Assembly code is literally a list of single instructions, one per line: an Instruction List.

front: Why can different IEC 61131-3 languages be used together in the same program?
back: All the languages share the standard's common elements, which define variables and function calls the same way for every language.
excerpt: The variables and function calls are defined by the common elements so different languages within the IEC 61131-3 standard can be used in the same program.

front: In a Function Block Diagram, how is one block's result passed on to another block?
back: A connection line joins the output of the first block to an input of the other block.
excerpt: Inputs and outputs of the blocks are wired together with connection lines or links.

front: In a Function Block Diagram, in which direction does a connection line carry its data?
back: From its left end to its right end; the connection is oriented.
excerpt: The connection is oriented, meaning that the line carries associated data from the left end to the right end.

front: In a Function Block Diagram, what must the left and right ends of a connection line have in common?
back: Both ends must be of the same type.
excerpt: The left and right ends of the connection line must be of the same type.

front: In a Function Block Diagram, what does a divergence (multiple right connection) do?
back: It broadcasts the information at its single left end to each of its several right ends.
excerpt: Multiple right connection, also called divergence, can be used to broadcast information from its left end to each of its right ends.
mnemonic: A river diverging: one stream in on the left, the same water out of every branch on the right.

front: How is program control flow achieved in Instruction List (IL)?
back: By jump instructions and function calls, which are subroutines with optional parameters.
excerpt: Program control (control flow) is achieved by jump instructions and function calls (subroutines with optional parameters).
